title: Geometric reducedness and transcendence degree in an algebraic field diamond
statement:
Let $k_0\subseteq k\subseteq E$ and $k_0\subseteq F\subseteq E$ be inclusions of fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]; $k$ and $F$ need not contain one another. Assume that $k/k_0$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], that $E/F$ is algebraic (every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $F$), and that for every extension field $K/k$ the ring $E\otimes_k K$ is reduced. Then for every extension field $L/k_0$ both $E\otimes_{k_0}L$ and $F\otimes_{k_0}L$ are reduced, and
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}F=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}E=\operatorname{trdeg}_kE.$$
Transcendence degrees use [def-kun-transcendence-degree], with cardinal lifts if needed. All tensor products are commutative algebra tensor products with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$. Reduced means having no nonzero nilpotent element. No finite generation, finite degree, group action, or geometric integrality hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-separable-scalar-restriction] with its smaller field $k=k_0$, larger field $k_1=k$, and algebra $A=E$. Its separable algebraic hypothesis is exactly the assumption on $k/k_0$, and its condition (2) is the assumed reducedness of $E\otimes_kK$ for every $K/k$. Condition (1) therefore gives reducedness of $E\otimes_{k_0}L$ for every $L/k_0$. The inclusions $k_0\subseteq k\subseteq E$ make $E$ a commutative $k$-algebra and its restricted $k_0$-structure is the given inclusion; the cited node requires no finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0C2Y, lemma-geometrically-reduced-over-separable-algebraic, forward paragraph of proof (restriction from k-prime to k)

proof.text: Fix any extension field $L/k_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], the $k_0$-vector space $L$ is flat. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] with $R=k_0$, $M=L$, $N=F$, $P=E$, and the $k_0$-linear inclusion $i:F\hookrightarrow E$. This makes $1\otimes i:L\otimes_{k_0}F\to L\otimes_{k_0}E$ injective. The swap $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$ is well defined by bilinearity and tensor balancing; swapping twice is the identity on pure tensors, hence on their sums. Compose the swap on $F\otimes_{k_0}L$, the injective map $1\otimes i$, and the swap on $L\otimes_{k_0}E$. This gives an injective ring map $j:F\otimes_{k_0}L\to E\otimes_{k_0}L$, $a\otimes b\mapsto i(a)\otimes b$: preservation of products follows on pure tensors from $i(aa')=i(a)i(a')$ and then by bilinearity. If $z^n=0$ with $n>0$, then $j(z)^n=0$; step 1 gives $j(z)=0$, and injectivity gives $z=0$. Thus $F\otimes_{k_0}L$ is reduced. This uses only $k_0\subseteq F\subseteq E$, without assuming $k\subseteq F$. The inclusion $F\hookrightarrow E$ is $k_0$-linear because both scalar actions are the specified inclusions of $k_0$ into these subfields of $E$.

source.place: lemma-subalgebra-separable, clause (1), and the tensor-injectivity observation immediately after lemma-geometrically-reduced-permanence; flat tensor injection supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Use [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] first for $k_0\subseteq F\subseteq E$. Since $E/F$ is algebraic, its zero-degree clause and tower formula give $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}E=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}F+0=\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}F$. Use the same node for $k_0\subseteq k\subseteq E$. The extension $k/k_0$ is algebraic, so the formula gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{k_0}E=0+\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=\operatorname{trdeg}_kE$. Combine the equalities. These are cardinal equalities, with lifts to a common universe when required; neither cancellation of an infinite cardinal nor finite generation is used. Both tower hypotheses hold because their structure homomorphisms are inclusions into the same field $E$; separability is used only in step 1, while this step uses the stated algebraicity assumptions.
